items.title: Voice Chat with Agents
items.excerpt: You can now talk with your agents in a realtime voice call. Describe a change out loud, ask what an agent is working on, and hear updates as the work moves forward. Voice chat works in the Agents Window, the IDE, on web, and in Cursor for iOS. Start a call When the agent is idle and the chat input is empty, click the waveform button labeled **Start voice chat**. It sits where Send usually is, next to the microphone button for dictation. On iOS, you can also say "Hey Siri, call Cursor" to start a call with a new agent, and mute or hang up from the Lock Screen with a Live Activity. Talk while the agent works The voice agent listens, replies, and hands coding work to the agent in your chat. While that agent runs, you can keep the conversation going. Ask what changed in a diff, check on a run, search earlier messages and calls with this agent, or switch between workers in a Project that has them. The coding agent speaks for itself too. It shares short progress notes while it works and a brief answer when it's done, so you usually hear a short update instead of the full written reply. Powered by Grok Voice Voice chat runs on Grok Voice. Pick from many voices in Voice settings, including Ara, Eve, Leo, Rex, and Sal. With Privacy Mode on, voice chat runs with zero data retention. Voice chat and dictation Voice chat is separate from dictation, which earlier releases called Voice Mode. Dictation still turns your speech into text in the chat input, and Cmd+Shift+Space still toggles it in the IDE. Voice chat is a two-way conversation where the agent answers out loud. Update Cursor to try voice chat. Learn more in our docs.
items.why_it_matters: Cursor adds realtime voice calls with agents across IDE, web and iOS. It is a notable AI coding tool feature that some engineers or clients may use, though it is not core to our Claude Code and Codex workflow.

items.title: Usage metrics API adds code review details and addressed rate
items.author: Allison
items.excerpt: The enterprise and organization repository-level Copilot usage metrics reports now show what happens to Copilot code review feedback. A new copilot_code_review object on each repos-1-day row reports how many Copilot-reviewed pull requests merged without a later change request from a person and how many Copilot code review comments developers acted on. With these you can track an addressed rate per repository. What’s new total_comments_evaluated: The number of Copilot code review comments checked to see whether the developer acted on them. total_comments_addressed: The number of evaluated comments the developer acted on, whether by applying the suggestion, asking Copilot to make the fix, editing the code, or replying that the fix will come in a later pull request. Divide by total_comments_evaluated for the addressed rate. review_comments_by_severity, review_comments_by_review_tier, review_comments_by_comment_type, and review_comments_by_customization: Both counts broken down by severity (e.g., high, medium, low), review tier (e.g., lite, balanced, max), comment type (e.g., bug, security, or custom for your repository’s own coding guidelines), and customization (e.g., custom instructions, skills, MCP servers, or none). total_merged_no_human_change_request_after_review: The number of merged pull requests that Copilot code review reviewed where no person requested changes after Copilot’s first review. Why this matters The existing pull_requests fields show how often Copilot code review runs and how often someone clicks to apply a suggestion, but developers act on most feedback in other ways. These fields show whether developers act on Copilot code review feedback in each repository, which kinds of comments land, whether custom instructions, skills, and MCP servers make a difference, and whether reviewers still request changes after Copilot reviews. Important notes Scope: Present on every row of the enterprise and organization repos-1-day reports. Counts are 0 and arrays
items.why_it_matters: Copilot code review addressed-rate metrics could help clients on Copilot measure AI review value. This touches verification of AI-assisted review, but Copilot is not our main tool.

items.title: Usage metrics API flags telemetry and version gaps
items.author: Allison
items.excerpt: The Copilot usage metrics API now shows which users are missing client telemetry or are running IDE or extension versions below the usage metrics minimums. New per-user fields appear in enterprise and organization user reports, and daily affected-user counts appear in enterprise and organization reports. What’s new client_telemetry_present: Whether client telemetry was received for the user that day. false means Copilot saw the user’s activity, but no usage events arrived from their editor. usage_metrics_requirements: Lists each of the user’s IDEs and Copilot extensions as met, unmet, or unknown against the minimum supported versions. missing_client_telemetry_user_count: The number of users that day with client_telemetry_present set to false. below_usage_metrics_minimum_user_count: The number of users that day with at least one IDE or extension below the minimum version. Why this matters Users without client telemetry still count as active, but their reports lack detail such as lines of code, feature breakdowns, and model breakdowns. Common causes include outdated editors or extensions, disabled IDE telemetry, and proxies or firewalls that block events. These fields show how many users are affected and who to follow up with. This way you can close gaps without opening a support ticket. Important notes Scope: User fields appear in enterprise and organization user reports (1-day and 28-day). Counts appear in enterprise and organization 1-day reports and in each day_totals entry of 28-day reports. Access: These fields are available to enterprise owners, enterprise billing managers, organization owners, and anyone with a custom organization or enterprise role that grants the View Copilot Metrics permission. The Copilot usage metrics policy must be enabled. Daily counts: Each count covers a single day. A user can be counted in both missing_client_telemetry_user_count and below_usage_metrics_minimum_user_count, so don’t add the two counts together. Don’t add counts across

items.title: Copilot impact dashboard adds chat and VS Code agent usage
items.author: Allison
items.excerpt: The Agent adoption chart in the Copilot impact dashboard now includes Copilot Chat and the VS Code Agents window, so you can see engagement across nine Copilot experiences. The adoption cohort called “Passive users” is now “Chat-first users”, which better describes who is in it. The enterprise and organization 28-day usage metrics reports include the same two features. This builds on feature engagement in the Copilot impact dashboard. What’s new Agent adoption chart: Adds Copilot Chat and the VS Code Agents window, for nine features in total. Chat-first users: Replaces the “Passive users” cohort name. These users are active in Copilot but haven’t used a qualifying feature on at least two days in the 28-day period, so they don’t qualify for an adoption phase. copilot_feature_engagement.totals_by_feature: Adds chat and vscode_agent entries to enterprise and organization 28-day reports. Why this matters Chat is a core Copilot experience, but the dashboard didn’t show it, and users who mainly use chat were labeled passive. Showing Copilot Chat and VS Code Agents window engagement and naming the cohort for what it represents gives a more complete picture of how developers use Copilot. Important notes Adoption phases are unchanged: Chat and the VS Code Agents window are reported as feature engagement but don’t count toward adoption phases. Chat-first users are still the No Cohort value in the API, and cohort sizes don’t change. Engagement rule: As with the other features, a user is engaged when they used the feature on at least two days in the 28-day period. A user can be counted under more than one feature. Chat covers Copilot Chat use captured by usage metrics, including agent mode, so users who make agent edits are also counted under chat. Scope: Like the other seven features, chat and the VS Code Agents window are only reported in enterprise and organization 28-day reports. items.title: v2.1.319
items.author: claude-code-publisher[bot]
items.excerpt: What's changed Changed auto mode with telemetry or feature flags off, including behind LLM gateways: calls the server can't check are asked about or denied, with no fallback to the built-in classifier; set CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=0 to keep using it (Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry are unchanged) Changed auto mode behind an LLM gateway: CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=1 turns on the server-side check even with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS set; if managed settings set the latter, they must set the 1 too Added support for MCP tasks in the terminal: when an MCP server runs a tool call as a task, Claude Code moves it to the background right away and tells Claude the result when it finishes Added the CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MCP_TASK_BACKGROUND environment variable to make Claude Code wait for an MCP task inside its tool call instead of moving it to the background right away Added permissions.denyInsteadOfPrompting setting: a tool call that would wait on a permission prompt is denied and the turn continues, in terminal sessions, subagents and teammates Added /claude-api latency-optimize to find where your Claude API code makes people wait and try faster settings against your eval Added the CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FEATURE_FLAGS environment variable, which stops feature-flag fetching without turning off telemetry; every flag then uses its built-in default Added spend for today, this week and this month to /usage for developers behind a Claude apps gateway who have no spend limit, when the gateway runs this version or later Added admin.pooled_conflict_rule and admin.pooled_priority_order to the Claude apps gateway, to set which pooled group budget pays first for a developer in several groups Added an optional login_notice setting to the Claude apps gateway that shows an operator-defined message on the gateway's browser verification page and on Claude Code's sign-in screen Added CLAUDE_GATEWAY_LOG_FORMAT=json to the Claude apps gateway: operational log lines become JSON with s

items.title: Controlling Biology - Fabian Theis, Helmholtz Munich
items.author: RJ Honicky
items.excerpt: Fabian Theis has been one of the key players in the various iterations of the Virtual Cell concept and initiatives. It is not hyperbole at all to say that his lab has been pushing the frontier of algorithms to understand multi-scale, multi-modal (”multiomics”), time-varying biological data. Indeed, he has shaped the large scale vision and data collection through his leadership at Helmholtz, various startups and probably at Biohub itself. Watch the full episode on YouTube… Much of the recent attention in AI x Bio has been on protein and molecular design. AlphaFold, ESM and BioHub, Chai, Leash, Isomporphic, Boltz, Genesis, Octant, Baker Lab, and many many more. After a lot of initial excitement, Virtual Cell projects have received less attention, due in no small part to questions about the effectiveness of large-scale models in solving even basic Virtual Cell problems. A $1.8B bet The Biohub announcement a few weeks ago got a lot of press for the (really) big numbers: $1.8B of commitments[1] from Biohub, NIH, DOE, Google and Meta. The discussion cites new imaging and measurement capabilities, generating large data sets and making the data available for training AI. View post on X ↗ But why are these organizations doubling down on these big bets now? They have been in the works for years now, what is going on that makes now the moment to push? New measurement capabilities and scale infrastructure, are now coming online that make Biohub’s push likely lead to big impact on science. DOE and NIH are developing lab-in-the-loop automation capabilities at scale. Google is scaling and broadening its connectomics capabilities ( episode coming soon!). Biohub itself has worked with various labs to develop and improve imaging platforms like laser phase plate microscopy, light sheet microscopy and advanced post-processing for regular microscopes that reveal deep phenotypic data. items.title: Quoting Nilay Patel
items.excerpt: The products aren't good enough to sell people on the costs. You cannot tell people that you have to listen to the whine of a data center in their backyard for AI overviews and some of the most hilarious deep fake slop in history. It's not worth it. It just isn't worth it to anyone. And agents aren't real and they might not be being used the way that anyone wants them to yet. All these companies are spending more than they're making on these products. Refrigerators holding blood storage in Europe are being hacked. The costs are too high. The benefits are not real. And if you connect that to corruption, you're like, in order to impose these costs on me, these CEOs are in the White House shaking Trump's hand, renaming it to the Gulf of America, paying for this ballroom that we don't want. It's obvious crypto-corruption, and it's still slop. The AI industry will not get out of it until they make better products. Until everyone can see without needing to be convinced, without needing an ad campaign, without any of this stuff that just using these products makes your life better. — Nilay Patel, The Vergecast: Big Tech lost big in the 2026 election Tags: nilay-patel, slop, ai, generative-ai, ai-ethics
